issues.body:
Re-verified at PR head. The PR updates every in-app copy surface for the new policy — the drawer header comment, the WEB_RDF_ACCEPT comment, DialogPrimitive.Description (~line 450), WebFilePane's paragraph and drop hint (~lines 727/731/767), status-bar.tsx:132, and engine-context.tsx — but gui/README.md is not in the diff at all (`git diff main --stat -- gui/` lists 7 files, no README).

gui/README.md:107 still reads: 'On the hosted web target, the drawer parses paste, file uploads, and URL responses in the in-tab WASM engine; compressed uploads and URL responses (`.gz` / `.zip` / `.zst` / `.bz2`) are decoded in the browser before parsing, while HDT remains native-only.'

After this change that exact scenario throws 'Bzip2 archives are supported only by the desktop app.' (file-decompress.ts:92-96). gui/README.md:103's `.gz` / `.bz2` / `.zst` mention is in the NATIVE-loader paragraph and is still true — leave it alone; import-drawer.tsx:899's native-pane copy is likewise still correct. skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md:259 describes @sparq/client, which retains bzip2, so it is also accurate.

A user-facing doc that advertises a capability the code now hard-rejects is an honesty defect under this repo's rules, not cosmetics — and it is the one gap in an otherwise exemplary doc-sync.
issues.fix_hint: Edit gui/README.md line 107 to match the new policy, e.g. '...compressed uploads and URL responses (`.gz` / `.zip` / `.zst`) are decoded in the browser before parsing, while bzip2 and HDT remain native-only.' Do not touch line 103 (native-loader paragraph — the native path really does stream .bz2). `grep -rn 'bz2\|bzip2' gui/` confirms README:107 is the only remaining web-scoped overclaim.
issues.title: UNFIXED from round 1: gui/README.md:107 still claims browser bzip2 decode that this PR removes

issues.body:
The diff carries a behaviour change beyond the bzip2 removal: IngestedFile gains `effectiveName` (file-ingest.ts:27), readFilesWithDecompress populates it from decoded.effectiveName (import-drawer.tsx:607), and import-drawer.tsx:270 now calls guessFormat(file.effectiveName ?? file.name). Nothing in the diff goes red if line 270 is reverted.

Re-verified the mechanism at head: gui/app/src/lib/rdf-format.ts:28 defines COMPRESSION_EXTS = {gz, bz2, zst, zstd}, so stripCompression('browser-upload.nt.zst') already yields 'browser-upload.nt' and guessFormat returns 'ntriples' from the OUTER name alone. The new e2e validates the zstd decode path (genuinely valuable — the fixture forces the real fzstd chunk to load) but is blind to the effectiveName wiring.

The case the fix actually repairs is ZIP: 'zip' is deliberately absent from COMPRESSION_EXTS, and packages/sparq-client/src/decompress.ts:283-292 returns the zip MEMBER name as innerName. So before this change 'bundle.zip' containing 'data.nq' produced guessFormat('bundle.zip') -> fallback 'turtle', handing N-Quads to the Turtle parser. That is exactly the regression effectiveName prevents, and it still has neither a unit nor an e2e test.
issues.fix_hint: Add a test that is red without the effectiveName change. Cheapest: a unit test in gui/app/src/lib/file-decompress.test.ts asserting the zip innerName mapping, plus the pure assertion guessFormat(result.effectiveName) === 'nquads' while guessFormat('bundle.zip') === 'turtle' — that pins the exact divergence. Alternatively extend the new e2e with a STORED-method zip fixture 'browser-upload.zip' whose single member is 'payload.nq' and assert the quad lands in the store; a STORED zip is hand-buildable (local header + data + central directory + EOCD) with no new dependency.
issues.title: UNFIXED from round 1: effectiveName plumbing still has no test that fails without it

issues.body:
file-decompress.ts:86-89 still tests only three bytes ('B','Z','h'):

    bytes.length >= 3 && bytes[0] === 0x42 && bytes[1] === 0x5a && bytes[2] === 0x68

Re-verified both existing implementations require the fourth byte to be the bzip2 block-size digit:
  * packages/sparq-client/src/decompress.ts:50-58 — `bytes[3] >= 0x31 && bytes[3] <= 0x39`
  * site/src/lib/rdf-import.ts isBzip2Source — the same four-byte test plus an `application/x-bzip2` Content-Type signal.

The divergence errs safe (it cannot MISS a real bzip2 stream), so this is not a wrong-answer bug, but any payload merely starting with the ASCII bytes 'BZh' is now hard-rejected with a bzip2-specific message instead of falling through to the uncompressed text path, and the GUI, the client library, and the site now disagree on what 'is bzip2' means — the kind of drift that bites a later refactor. The Content-Type signal is also absent here; for fetchRdfDocument a server sending application/x-bzip2 is caught by the magic check in practice, so that part is a consistency point rather than a hole.
issues.fix_hint: Tighten to the four-byte form used elsewhere (`bytes.length >= 4 && ... && bytes[3] >= 0x31 && bytes[3] <= 0x39`). Better: export the existing detector instead of writing a third copy — lift site/src/lib/rdf-import.ts's isBzip2Source into @sparq/client next to codecFromMagic and import it here, and reuse CODEC_EXTENSIONS.bzip2 (['bz2','bzip2','tbz','tbz2'], decompress.ts:33) instead of re-listing the suffixes inline at file-decompress.ts:90-92.
issues.title: UNFIXED from round 1: bzip2 magic check omits the version-digit byte, diverging from the two existing detectors

issues.body:
The fixture at line 103-106 is still `new FakeFile('dataset.nt.bz2', [0x42,0x5a,0x68,0x39])` — the name ends in .bz2 AND the bytes carry BZh9. isBzip2 (file-decompress.ts:85-92) is an OR of those two signals, so the assertion still passes if either branch is deleted. The test proves the gate exists but not that both halves work, which matters because the extension branch guards a mislabelled/short payload and the magic branch guards a renamed archive.

Not vacuous (it asserts a real rejection on the real path and pins the error string), just under-discriminating relative to the surrounding tests — this file already models an explicit non-vacuity/mutation test at lines 62-77.
issues.fix_hint: Split into two cases: (a) magic-only — FakeFile('dataset.nt', [0x42,0x5a,0x68,0x39]) must reject, proving the extension is not required; (b) extension-only — FakeFile('dataset.nt.bz2', <plain UTF-8 N-Triples bytes>) must reject, proving the name signal alone fires. Optionally add a negative guard that a plain file whose bytes start 'BZh' followed by a NON-digit still decodes as text, pinning whichever magic width is chosen for the issue above.
issues.title: UNFIXED from round 1: new bzip2 test conflates both detection branches, so it cannot catch removal of either

issues.body:
WEB_RDF_ACCEPT still loses `.tgz` alongside `.bz2`/`.bzip2`, and file-decompress.ts's header comment drops its `.tgz` mention too, with no comment, copy string, or PR text explaining it — every other line of the diff is about bzip2.

On the merits the removal is defensible: @sparq/client maps 'tgz' -> gzip (decompress.ts:30) and innerNameForSource returns null for tgz (decompress.ts:87), so decompressing a .tgz yields TAR bytes the RDF parser rejects anyway. Worth noting the accept list only constrains the file PICKER — handleDrop (import-drawer.tsx:683) does no extension filtering, so a dragged .tgz still reaches decompressDatasetBytes and produces a confusing parse error rather than an honest 'tar archives are not supported' message. That drop-path gap pre-dates this PR.
issues.fix_hint: Either restore `.tgz` to keep the diff strictly bzip2-scoped, or keep the removal and add one line to the WEB_RDF_ACCEPT comment saying tar containers (.tgz/.tbz) are unsupported because decompression yields a TAR stream, not RDF. Making the drop path say so too is a separate bead, not work for this PR.
issues.title: UNFIXED from round 1: `.tgz` silently dropped from WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, outside the PR's stated bzip2 scope

verdict.summary:
Round 2 is byte-for-byte the same change as round 1: `git diff main --stat -- gui/` still shows exactly 7 files (import-drawer.tsx, status-bar.tsx, engine-context.tsx, file-decompress.ts, file-decompress.test.ts, file-ingest.ts, browser-upload.web.spec.ts) and NONE of the five prior findings has been addressed. No new code was pushed, so nothing regressed either — hence "stagnant".

The underlying change remains directionally sound: maybeDecompressBytes throws "Bzip2 archives are supported only by the desktop app." before decompressDatasetBytes, both ingest entry points (handleInputChange picker and the custom handleDrop, which does no extension pre-filter) funnel through readFilesWithDecompress and surface the throw as a per-file `rejected` reason, and the URL tab surfaces it via finishImport. The hand-built zstd fixture is spec-correct (RFC 8878 magic 28 b5 2f fd, descriptor 0x20, 3-byte raw last-block header, <=255 guard) so it really exercises the lazy fzstd decoder.

Still blocking:

(1) gui/README.md:107 verified stale at PR head — it still tells users web "compressed uploads and URL responses (`.gz` / `.zip` / `.zst` / `.bz2`) are decoded in the browser before parsing". After this PR a .bz2 upload/fetch throws. Every other copy surface was updated; this one user-facing doc now overclaims a capability the PR deliberately removes. (README:103 and import-drawer.tsx:899 are native-loader copy and remain correct; skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md:259 describes @sparq/client itself, which keeps bzip2 — also correct.)

(2) The effectiveName plumbing (file-ingest.ts:27, import-drawer.tsx:270/607) is a real functional fix with no test that fails without it. Verified: rdf-format.ts:28 COMPRESSION_EXTS includes "zst", so guessFormat("browser-upload.nt.zst") already yields "ntriples" from the outer name — the new e2e passes byte-identically after reverting line 270 to guessFormat(file.name).
